name: Duraveil-GX
description: A woven graphene-fiber textile composite developed by Veilweave Textiles in partnership with Apex Nanofabrication, produced by weaving continuous graphene-coated polymer filaments into dense, tightly interlocked fabric structures. Unlike film-based graphene materials, Duraveil-GX retains textile drape and garment-manufacturing compatibility while delivering surface conductivity, EMI shielding, and cut resistance that no conventional fabric can match. The material is available in several weave densities from lightweight signal-shielding liners to heavy-duty protective outerwear.
applications: EMI-shielded garments for sensitive electronics operators
cut-resistant work garments for industrial environments
conductive textile interfaces for wearable electronics
Faraday-cage lining for secure meeting rooms and transport
story_hooks: Duraveil-GX signal-blocking garments have become essential equipment for people trying to move through the city without being tracked — which means a thriving black market has emerged in knockoff versions that provide a false sense of security while leaking data.

A Veilweave Textiles production manager approaches a fixer with evidence that Duraveil-GX garments sold to a government security contractor have been secretly modified with additional conductive pathways that could be used for remote biometric monitoring of the wearers.

The combination of Duraveil-GX's cut resistance and signal shielding has made it the preferred material for a new generation of professional thieves who can move through secure facilities without triggering proximity sensors or leaving clean forensic traces.
